label: input token u during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter u, but only while the original sequence is being read. It fires on every original-phase step whose input is u (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.996) and on no other input token. It does NOT fire on the <DEL> step, and almost never fires on u when u is fed back during the copy phase (~395 weak activations, nearly all at recall_idx 1). Magnitude depends on position: it is largest when u is the first token (t=0, about 1.0 of max) and falls off for later positions (late-position u often 0.2-0.65 of max). Magnitude is also lower for a repeated u than for the first occurrence of u in the sequence, though repeats still fire. The adjacent tokens and the length L have little effect on whether it fires.

issues: Minor: there are 375 test misses (0.0% of activation mass). All are tiny activations (0.00-0.09 of max) on u fed back in the copy phase at recall_idx 1, i.e. when orig(0)==u. This is the weak copy-phase tail the explanation already describes, not a gap. On the dev split, copy-phase u fires on only 0.43% of its steps.

Minor imprecision in the magnitude claim: steps in the middle of the sequence typically reach 0.8-0.9 of max. Lower values of 0.5-0.65 show up mostly at late positions (t>=5) and on repeated u (as low as 0.2). The overall claim of 'largest at t=0, decreasing with position' holds.
Repeated u (in_first==0) fires with precision 1.0 (10,093 of 10,093 dev steps), which confirms 'repeats still fire'. Precision is 1.0 with 0 test false positives. Delimiter-step activation is 0.
